detailed_description: The Sunburst Chart Generator is a specialized data visualization tool that transforms hierarchical datasets into radial partition diagrams. By mapping parent-child relationships through concentric rings, this tool enables users to represent multi-level categorical data with proportional segments whose arc lengths correspond to their quantitative value. Built using D3.js and HTML5 Canvas, it supports real-time rendering of complex hierarchies containing thousands of nodes while maintaining SVG scalability for detailed exports. Users can leverage this tool for business intelligence reporting, system resource analysis, and content taxonomy mapping where spatial relationships between nested categories require visual clarification. The generator implements a weighted recursive partitioning algorithm that calculates radial dimensions based on value ratios at each hierarchy level, allowing precise control over angular distribution and depth perception through gradient color encoding. Technical features include drag-and-drop CSV/JSON file import, custom color palette integration, and adjustable radius scaling to emphasize specific data tiers. Interactive previews with hover tooltips displaying node metadata enhance analytical capabilities before final export.
usage_steps: Import structured data via drag-and-drop file uploader (CSV/JSON) containing hierarchical key-value pairs
Define hierarchy depth using the level configuration panel to assign categorical tiers to concentric rings
Select color encoding method (categorical, sequential, or diverging) from the palette manager for segment differentiation
Adjust radius scale multiplier in the layout settings to control visual emphasis on inner/outer hierarchy levels
Enable interactive features like tooltip display or zoom functionality through the behavior toggle menu
Export final visualization using resolution-preserving SVG download or PNG screenshot capture buttons
usage_examples: Visualizing enterprise organizational structure with departments as primary rings and employee distribution as secondary segments
Analyzing website traffic sources through nested layers showing referral channels, subdomains, and individual page performance
Mapping computer storage usage with top-level directories as outer rings and file-type breakdowns in inner segments
Demonstrating product category sales distribution across multiple geographic regions with color-coded revenue proportionality
